news.title: Dutch football association backed FIFA president Infantino before reversing its position
news.lede: The Dutch Football Association (KNVB) initially backed Gianni Infantino's bid to remain FIFA president, even though it later withdrew its support for him. Secretary-general Gijs de Jong disclosed that the KNVB had personally handed Infantino a letter endorsing his candidacy shortly before changing its position. "The letter had no legal value whatsoever. At that moment, it was a strategic decision in the interests of Dutch football," De Jong said.

news.title: Spain thought it had the 2030 World Cup final, yet Morocco had other plans
news.lede: MADRID/RABAT: When Spain won a joint bid to host the 2030 World Cup, officials at the national football association took it as given that the final would be held on their soil. As former world champions – a feat since repeated – and the world’s second-most visited country, Spain had the sporting pedigree and tourism know-how to welcome large crowds, so it was widely assumed the final would come to them. Co-host Portugal was not interested, while Spanish officials thought that Morocco, as a late addition to the bid, surely would not agitate for the final. But in recent months Spain has begun to fear that the North African nation, an emerging football power, could snatch the game’s biggest showpiece from under its nose.
